message:
release: 0.2.148 (PC) and APK 0.2.25 -- the bitrate you set is what the video uses on the wire

PC (Windows). The user's bitrate is now the ceiling for the whole video stream on the wire -- data,
FEC parity, NACK replays and the UDP/IP headers through one shared limiter -- instead of a mean the
encoder was asked to keep (on 0.2.147 a 6 Mbps setting measured 13.6 Mbps at the host). An input gate
before the encoder keeps the queue bounded, replays are served by the sender within the same budget
and only for their own session, and a key frame is tracked by its media/generation/input epoch.
Measured on real MFT + decoder: every 1 s and 250 ms window <= cap + 10% (6M/60 motion 101.0/103.7,
1.5M/30 100.8/103.1, 5% loss with NACK storm 101.0/103.7, a 6->1.5 downshift from its applied point).
Runtime click-to-screen is unchanged (event-ID paired: cap on == cap off == 0.2.147 source); a full
screen change and the first picture after connect take longer, by the time their bytes need at the cap.
Kill switch REMOTE60_NATIVE_WIRE_CAP=0.

APK (shared receiver code): a large frame still arriving is not counted lost while its chunks keep
coming (progress-based NACK tail), so a paced key frame no longer draws premature NACKs.

Feat: bitrate-hard-cap r1..r9 (24b8bf6 .. ef81624; product 152b685, after it tests only).
Verified: verifier's independent builds and runs at every round (last: real-recv smoke 12/12 on the
product receiver path, matrix 155/0, paired 118/0 with an independently built a95215e host); main
integration (fresh configure) 19 suites + real-recv + matrix exit 0; Codex source OK + release go.
Not verified: the field run between two PCs and over WAN at 6 Mbps; host-side handling of the
viewer's key request in the loss-free initial/idle case (observed, not round-tripped).

Product: version only (PC 0.2.147 -> 0.2.148; APK versionName 0.2.23 -> 0.2.25, versionCode 22 -> 24 -- main
never carried APK 0.2.24, which was released from its own branch at versionCode 23). Test: none. Docs: none.
